entry.description:
Rule 210, the two-sided statement: no finite configuration keeps the period-2 clock on its center column. The primary source reports: For rule 210, $x' = \ell \oplus (\lnot c \wedge r)$, no finite configuration keeps the period-2 clock on its center column: if $x_0 : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathrm{Bool}$ is white outside a bounded interval and $\mathrm{run210}\,x_0\,t\,0 = [t \text{ odd}]$ for every $t$, then false (`Rule30Submission.no_finite_clock`). Hence no finite configuration has an eventually alternating center column in either phase (`no_finite_eventually_alternating`), and the kit's seed does not (`seed_not_eventually_alternating`, through `run210_seed`).

The catalog's `Rule30ZeroBoundary.Q01` is the period-2 question for rule 30 in one-sided form, and `Rule30Realization.barrier` shows that rules 90, 150 and 210 share left-permutivity and Jen's theorem with rule 30. Our submission R30-20261022-920c1b showed the one-sided statement false for rule 210: the empty left half keeps the clock. This essay proves the two-sided statement true, so for rule 210 the finite-configuration form of period 2 holds while the zero-boundary form fails.

Under the clock every black cell of the left half has $t + k$ even (`parity_left_of_clock`), so the left half is parity-sparse and evolves as rule 90. Each admissible left row has a parity-sparse clock realization (`clock_bg`); a finite configuration either equals one, where rule 90's freshman's dream $x_{2^n} = x \oplus \sigma^{2^n} x$ breaks the clock at time $2^n + 1$ (`no_finite_clock90`), or first deviates from it at some depth, and a clearing front then carries the deviation to the center column at a computed time (`Dev.odd_impossible`, `Dev.even_impossible`).

Nothing is claimed about rule 30 itself, nor about infinite configurations of rule 210. entry.description:
The channel bound at width 14: explicit automaton states, one kernel check per state. The primary source reports: For every configuration $x : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathrm{Bool}$ whose center column reads the clock, $\mathrm{evol}\,x\,t\,0 = [t \text{ odd}]$ for all $t$, the first $n$ visible bits $\mathrm{visFrom}\,x\,0\,n$ (column $1$ at the even times) lie in one set $S$ of words with $|S| \cdot 10^{9n} \le 300 \cdot 1184655442^{\,n}$ (`Rule30Submission.channel_bound_14`): about $0.2445$ bits of information per visible bit asymptotically ($\log_2(1184655442/10^9) \approx 0.24447$, with a finite correction $\log_2 300 / n$).

The catalog reduces period 2 to `Rule30ZeroBoundary.Q01` and has nothing about the right neighbour of a clocked column. Our submission R30-20261023-4767e0 proved this bound at width $12$ ($0.258$ bits) by rebuilding the window automaton inside one kernel computation; that does not scale, since the kernel's caches live for one declaration. Here the certificate is explicit: the bitset of each of the $919$ states of the width-$14$ automaton, its graph and Collatz-Wielandt weights.

One theorem per state (`s14_i`) has the kernel sweep the state's bitset and check that every member's four two-step images, with the cell beyond the window at the two successive times as free inputs, lie in the successor of its label (`stateCheck`); `explicit_sound` assembles the $919$ theorems into the closure of every edge, `bound_of` and `weight_bound` give the bound, and `win_step2` ties the window to the kit's `evol`. The sets are checked data, not derived: any family with the root full and every edge closed bounds the words.

Nothing here decides `Q01`: the bound measures the right neighbour. Width $16$ (about $0.2131$ bits) would need about $45$ MB of state literals in this form and is not attempted. For every configuration $x : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathrm{Bool}$ whose center column reads the clock, $\mathrm{evol}\,x\,t\,0 = [t \text{ odd}]$ for all $t$, the first $n$ visible bits $\mathrm{visFrom}\,x\,0\,n$ (column $1$ at the even times) lie in one set $S$ of words with $|S| \cdot 10^{9n} \le 300 \cdot 1184655442^{\,n}$ (`Rule30Submission.channel_bound_14`): about $0.2445$ bits of information per visible bit asymptotically ($\log_2(1184655442/10^9) \approx 0.24447$, with a finite correction $\log_2 300 / n$).

The catalog reduces period 2 to `Rule30ZeroBoundary.Q01` and has nothing about the right neighbour of a clocked column. Our submission R30-20261023-4767e0 proved this bound at width $12$ ($0.258$ bits) by rebuilding the window automaton inside one kernel computation; that does not scale, since the kernel's caches live for one declaration. Here the certificate is explicit: the bitset of each of the $919$ states of the width-$14$ automaton, its graph and Collatz-Wielandt weights.

One theorem per state (`s14_i`) has the kernel sweep the state's bitset and check that every member's four two-step images, with the cell beyond the window at the two successive times as free inputs, lie in the successor of its label (`stateCheck`); `explicit_sound` assembles the $919$ theorems into the closure of every edge, `bound_of` and `weight_bound` give the bound, and `win_step2` ties the window to the kit's `evol`. The sets are checked data, not derived: any family with the root full and every edge closed bounds the words.

Nothing here decides `Q01`: the bound measures the right neighbour. Width $16$ (about $0.2131$ bits) would need about $45$ MB of state literals in this form and is not attempted.

entry.description:
Two More Eventual Words Excluded from the Center Column of Rule 30. The primary source reports: For the single-seed evolution of rule 30, the center column is not eventually the repeating word $0^9\,1$, nor the repeating word $0^7\,1\,0\,1\,1$, whatever the transient and the phase: `Rule30Submission.not_eventually_0000000001` and `Rule30Submission.not_eventually_00000001011` prove `¬ EventuallyWord w` for these two words.

What is new: `Rule30StripCertificateTable` excludes thirty words of lengths 8 to 13, and `Rule30StripCertificates` the rank-certificate words $0^6\,1\,1$ and $0^9\,1\,0\,1$; neither word here is among them, in any rotation. `Rule30WhiteEnd` excludes $1\,0^q$ for every $q \ge 10$ and claims nothing for $q \le 9$; its `control_q9` shows that its check fails at $q = 9$. The first word is exactly that case.

Method: each proof is a rank certificate in the format of `Rule30StripCertificates.Cert` (strip width 12 with 40,010 ranks for the first word, width 6 with 552 ranks for the second), found by computer search and checked by the Lean kernel with `decide +kernel`. The kit's soundness theorem `Cert.not_eventuallyWord`, through masked Jen, gives the exclusion.

Nothing is claimed for the words $1\,0^q$ with $q \le 8$, for other words, or for Problem 1 itself. entry.description:
Sparse16: A Finite Obstruction to an Alternating Center in Rule 30. The primary source reports: For every Boolean half-line $L$, if the official zero-boundary Rule 30 evolution is black at depth 1 at all 56 even times $0,2,\ldots,110$, then at least 17 of $L(1),\ldots,L(111)$ are black. The farther initial tail is unrestricted. This is the theorem `Rule30Submission.PortableSparse16.fifty_six_even_black_forces_seventeen`. Its corollaries include an even white observation for every prefix of weight at most 16, and a necessary left-prefix weight for a whole-line configuration whose center alternates from time zero.

The primary source reports: The kit's Rule30ZeroBoundaryWidth52 proves that every zero-boundary start supported at depths at most 52 has a white depth-1 cell at some even time at most 96, and says of 96 that its tightness is observed, not proved. This essay proves the tightness: the explicit start 0x7dc2ff6fcc4fd is black at depth 1 at every even time below 96 and white at 96, by the kit's packed evaluator prun and its bridge run_toFun, so the death time at width 52 is exactly 96 (the headline theorem Rule30Submission.death_time_52_exact). Two further explicit starts give the lower bounds 100 at width 56 and 114 at width 60 (width56_lower, width60_lower); in our record both are exact by complete chunk certificates at K = 101 and K = 115, which are not carried here. The primary source reports: For the general left-permutive cellular automaton family `run (g : Bool -> Bool -> Bool)` in `Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30Realization`, Jen's adjacent-column theorem `run_not_adjacent` assumes `g false false = false` and `g false true = true`. We prove that a Boolean function `g` satisfies these two hypotheses if and only if `g = g90 \lor g = g150 \lor g = g210 \lor g = g30` (`Rule30Submission.jen_class_iff_four_rules`). Within this four-element class, we prove three exact equivalences for the single-seed evolution `run g`: (1) `\forall t\,p,\, run g t p = run g90 t p` holds if and only if `g = g90 \lor g = g210` (`Rule30Submission.run_eq_run90_iff_g90_or_g210`); (2) the single-seed pattern is mirror-symmetric (`\forall t\,p,\, run g t (-p) = run g t p`) if and only if `g = g90 \lor g = g150 \lor g = g210` (`Rule30Submission.run_symm_iff_not_g30`); and (3) the center column `fun t => run g t 0` is not eventually constant (`\lnot \exists T\,b,\, \forall t \ge T,\, run g t 0 = b`) if and only if `g = g30` (`Rule30Submission.g30_unique_nonconstant_in_jen_class`).

entry.description: Telling left edges apart from the center column: exact deadlines for three edge pairs. The primary source reports: For any two configurations x, y of rule 30 whose leftmost black cells sit at -2 and -1, the center columns differ at some time t <= 8 (sep_8); for leftmost black cells at -4 and -3 by time 13 (sep_13), at -3 and -2 by time 14 (sep_14); each bound is attained (attained_8, attained_13, attained_14). The right side is unrestricted, finite or infinite. The kit's later module Rule30TraceEdge names the conjecture that two finite configurations with the same complete center trace have the same left edge and proves that it implies Problem 1; these are three exact negative-edge cases of the conjecture, for every configuration with those edges. The center through time m depends on the initial cells at positions at most m only, so a configuration is cut to the window [a, m]; the 2^(m - a) fillings with a black cell at a run as lanes of one number, the signatures of each edge class are collected into a bitset, and the bitsets are disjoint, checked by the kernel in blocks of 256 values. Nothing is claimed about the general conjecture or Problem 1. entry.description: Two infinite families of right halves absorbed by the ether: CQ01 for every right half with one of two prefixes. The primary source reports: The kit's coupled question CQ01 holds iff for every finite right half R the sideways row Psi R, the constrained start whose free bits complement column 1 of R driven by the alternating column, has infinitely many black cells; it holds for R whenever that column is eventually periodic (the kit's absorption route), and the milestone R = empty is open. For R31, black cells 1..5, and R495, black cells 1..4 and 6..9 (the row of R31 at time 4), the driven right half enters the kit's ether-and-wall trap: at time 9, respectively 5, columns 1..6 carry the kit's 7 x 4 ether with the alternating column as its column B4, and columns 7..19 are one of the kit's 109 wall states. Radius-one locality carries this entry to every right half that agrees with R31 on cells 1..28, or with R495 on cells 1..24, whatever its later cells, and the kit's trap invariant keeps the ether for ever, so all of them have the parity of the step as their visible column. Hence CQ01 for every finite member of the two families (CQ01_prefix31, CQ01_prefix495), among them the pairwise distinct right halves R31 plus one black cell at 29 + n (CQ01_fam, fam_injective), all with one sideways row (Psi_prefix31, Psi_prefix495, Psi_eq). The seeds are not joined by the right-end moves, the inverse of the kit's terminal rewrites 011 -> 01 and 101 -> 11 (not_move_equivalent). Nothing is claimed about CQ01 in general, the empty right half, or Problem 1. entry.description: A three-fifths bound on black runs in the rule 30 center column. The primary source reports: We prove in Lean that a black run of the rule 30 center column lasts at most about three fifths of its starting time: if c(a) = … = c(a + L − 1) = 1 with a ≥ 1, then L ≤ a − 2⌊(a − 1)/5⌋, hence 5L ≤ 3a + 10 (headline `Rule30Submission.black_run_three_fifths`). The kit's catalog had L ≤ a (`Rule30CenterRuns.black_run_le`). As consequences, every window [a, (8a + 10)/5] contains a white cell, so there are about log_{8/5} n white cells before time n, where the catalog had ⌊log₄ n⌋; the argument also bounds alternating blocks anywhere in the light cone and, relative to the first black cell right of the center, white runs. Under a black run the row at time a alternates. Going back in time, left-permutivity rebuilds each earlier row from the later one and two unknown cells; whatever those cells are, the alternation heals four cells further out, so after s steps the row alternates on cells 4s to L − 1 + s left of the center. After ⌊(a − 1)/5⌋ steps this block would contain the two adjacent black cells of the left edge, which is impossible. The four-cell healing is in `Rule30ZeroBoundaryStripe.agrees_pre`; what is new is its use on a finite block together with the left edge. We claim no unconditional bound of slope below 1 for white runs, and nothing sublinear: 3/5 is the limit of this method. entry.description:
Period-32 two-phase shielding rigidity for finite Rule 30 moving-front states. The primary source reports: Let $D(x)_k = x_k \oplus (x_{k+1} \lor x_{k+2})$ be the triangular map of `Rule30ControlledResponse`: the right half of rule 30 seen in a frame moving one cell per step. For every state $x : \mathbb{N} \to \{0,1\}$ that is zero from some cell $W$ on, if $D^{32}x = x$ and the alternating shielding gates hold (for every $t < 32$, $(D^t x)_0 \lor (D^t x)_1$ when $t$ is even and $(D^t x)_0$ when $t$ is odd), then $D^2 x = x$ (`Rule30Submission.period_thirtytwo_reduces_to_two`). For an integer $n$ with $T(n) = n \oplus ((n \gg 1) \lor (n \gg 2))$, $T^{32}(n) = n$ and the same gates on its bits, $n$ is a canonical stripe $U_w$ for some $w$ (`Rule30Submission.period_thirtytwo_gate_stripe`). No bound on the width $W$ is assumed.

The catalog's `Rule30FiniteClockCertificate` proves generic soundness of finite temporal-profile pools, and `Rule30FiniteClockSixteen` applies it to full clocks dividing 16. This applies it at clock 32 under the gates and adds the stripe classification.

Method: a pool of 2,116 temporal pairs of 32-periodic columns, closed under left extension and checked by the kernel in 67 blocks, covers every finite width. On gated pairs the head has period 2, and a detection check carries that clock to the whole state. A 14-state certificate over an eight-state stripe automaton then identifies the period-2 integer profiles as stripes.

Not claimed: the result is conditional on the 32-step return and on the gates. It excludes no period of the center column and solves no Rule 30 Prize problem. entry.description:
Unconditional Six-Cell and Seven-Cell Stripe-Tail Mortality and Sparse Return-Map Completion of (97, 0) in Zero-Boundary Rule 30. The primary source reports: We extend the zero-boundary stripe-prefix mortality hierarchy in WolframInstitute/Rule30PrizeKit from five tail cells (`v : Fin 32`, 64 classes) to all six-cell (`v : Fin 64`, 128 classes) and seven-cell (`v : Fin 128`, 256 classes) stripe-prefix tails in core Lean 4.35.0:

1. Variable-Width Front-Window Compression (15.5x orbit reduction): Certifying each non-exceptional front window `(w, 0)` at its minimal valid width `K in [8, 30]` (`S = K - 1 <= 29 < 31`) reduces the 16 six-cell front windows (`cyc6_33`..`cyc6_63` in `Rule30Certificates/ZeroBoundaryStripeCycles4`) from 589,824 steps at `K = 32` to 62,848 steps (6.11 s, 0.28 GB RSS), and the 31 non-exceptional seven-cell front windows (`cyc7_65`..`cyc7_127`, `w != 97`, in `Rule30Certificates/ZeroBoundaryStripeCycles5`) from 1,179,648 steps to 51,008 steps (5.29 s, 0.27 GB RSS).

2. Discovery and Completion of `(97, 0)`: Across all odd front windows up to 7 bits (`w in 1..127`), `(97, 0)` is the unique new window after `(13, 0)` that fails to close at `K <= 34`. entry.description: Least Period 4 of Rule 30: a Weaker Sufficient Condition, and Why the Left Half Must Be Finite. The primary source reports: Problem 1 asks whether the center column of rule 30 is ever eventually periodic. The kit reduces the three words of least period 4 (0001, 0011, 0111) to the open statement Absorption (Rule30Ether): every finite right half driven by the word must eventually enter a family of ether-and-wall states. The kit's proof only uses a consequence of that entry, which we isolate as Lock w: every finite right half driven by w^∞ has column 1 eventually periodic at the white times of the driver (with any period 4Q), or some column q ≥ 1 eventually periodic. We prove in Lean that Lock w excludes w^∞ as a tail of the center column whatever the transient (Rule30Submission.lock_excludes, by masked Jen or by Jen), that the kit's Absorption implies Lock (lock_of_absorption), and that the three locks exclude least period 4 (least_period_four_of_lock). Lock is open for the three words, but it no longer mentions the ether, the wall or any entry state. Second, the proof uses the finiteness of the left half (through Jen), and that hypothesis cannot be weakened to spatial periodicity, even with a finite right half: for each of the three words, and for the alternating column 1, 0, 1, 0, …, there is a configuration whose left half is the 7-periodic ether and whose right half is finite (ether columns, one of the kit's wall states, then white), with center column exactly the word from time 0 (period_four_left_periodic_right_finite, alt_left_periodic_right_finite). The kit's ether_coupled_witness had both halves infinite. Numerically, every right half of width ≤ 24 locks for the three words, the locking time does not depend on the width, and among the words of period ≤ 7 these three are the only ones whose driven right halves locked for every finite right half we tested, so Lock is a statement about period 4 only. entry.description: Rule 30, Period 2: a Closed Trap for the Right Half Driven from the Empty Row. The primary source reports: Problem 1 asks whether the center column of rule 30 is ever eventually periodic. For period 2 the kit has the coupled question CQ01 (no configuration with finitely many black cells has center column 1, 0, 1, 0, … from time 0): for every finite right half R there is exactly one candidate left row Psi R, whose free bits are the complement of u R, column 1 of the right half R driven by the alternating column, read at the white steps; CQ01 holds iff Psi R is infinite for every finite R, and the milestone CQ01Empty, the case R = ∅, is open. We prove in Lean that u ∅ follows the ether (gaps 2 and 5) and then, from s = 146 on and for ever, has gaps 3 or 5 between consecutive black cells (Rule30Submission.u_empty_gaps): the windows of columns 1..16 at the odd steps form a set of 829 windows that is closed under the double step whatever column 17 does, and inside it the gaps are 3 or 5 (kernel checks), and the window of R = ∅ enters it at step 293. The same holds for every right half whose window enters the trap (gaps_of_entry); numerically 96 % of random finite right halves enter it, and the others have u eventually periodic, a case the kit already settles. Spacing 3 or 5 of such a gate is the hypothesis that the kit's recent modules on gates assume without claiming it for any finite right half; we prove it for R = ∅ from s = 146 on (`u_empty_window` for `Rule30DrivenPrefix.Window`, `u_empty_spaced` for `Rule30SpacingRenormalization.Spaced`), and that the transformed gate is not spaced, so their eight-column translation cannot be iterated on it (`u_empty_transform_not_spaced`). This turns CQ01Empty into a left-only statement weaker than the kit's Q01: Q01Gap, no finitely supported constrained start of the zero-boundary left half has free bits that are eventually the complement of a concatenation of 001 and 00001. We prove Q01 ⇒ Q01Gap, Q01Gap ⇒ ¬ FinSupp (Psi R) for every R entering the trap (not_finSupp_Psi_of_Q01Gap), hence Q01Gap ⇒ CQ01Empty (CQ01Empty_of_Q01Gap). Q01Gap is open; nothing here excludes period 2. For period 2 the kit has the coupled question CQ01 (no configuration with finitely many black cells has center column 1, 0, 1, 0, … from time 0): for every finite right half R there is exactly one candidate left row Psi R, whose free bits are the complement of u R, column 1 of the right half R driven by the alternating column, read at the white steps; CQ01 holds iff Psi R is infinite for every finite R, and the milestone CQ01Empty, the case R = ∅, is open. We prove in Lean that u ∅ follows the ether (gaps 2 and 5) and then, from s = 146 on and for ever, has gaps 3 or 5 between consecutive black cells (Rule30Submission.u_empty_gaps): the windows of columns 1..16 at the odd steps form a set of 829 windows that is closed under the double step whatever column 17 does, and inside it the gaps are 3 or 5 (kernel checks), and the window of R = ∅ enters it at step 293. The same holds for every right half whose window enters the trap (gaps_of_entry); numerically 96 % of random finite right halves enter it, and the others have u eventually periodic, a case the kit already settles. Spacing 3 or 5 of such a gate is the hypothesis that the kit's recent modules on gates assume without claiming it for any finite right half; we prove it for R = ∅ from s = 146 on (`u_empty_window` for `Rule30DrivenPrefix.Window`, `u_empty_spaced` for `Rule30SpacingRenormalization.Spaced`), and that the transformed gate is not spaced, so their eight-column translation cannot be iterated on it (`u_empty_transform_not_spaced`). This turns CQ01Empty into a left-only statement weaker than the kit's Q01: Q01Gap, no finitely supported constrained start of the zero-boundary left half has free bits that are eventually the complement of a concatenation of 001 and 00001. We prove Q01 ⇒ Q01Gap, Q01Gap ⇒ ¬ FinSupp (Psi R) for every R entering the trap (not_finSupp_Psi_of_Q01Gap), hence Q01Gap ⇒ CQ01Empty (CQ01Empty_of_Q01Gap). entry.description: Rule 30: Self-Shielded Black Runs, Sharper White-Run Bounds, and Q01 as an Integer Iteration. The primary source reports: Problem 1 asks whether the center column of rule 30 is ever eventually periodic. We prove three partial results in Lean, against the current kit. **Self-shielding.** By the kit's Lemma A* (`Rule30BlackRuns.black_shield`), a black run of length 9j in the center column forces the pattern (white, black)^j in columns 1..2j. This pattern shields itself: it moves two columns to the right every two steps without reading the cell on its right, so for 2j steps after the run the columns 1..2j depend only on the center column, and column 1 is determined for 4j steps instead of the 2j of the light cone. With masked Jen this halves the slope of the kit's Theorems B and D: if the center column is eventually P-periodic, it has no black run of length r < P followed by a white cell with 9⌈(P−r)/4⌉ ≤ r (`Rule30Submission.no_long_black_run_quarter`; the kit needs 9⌈(P−r+9)/2⌉ ≤ r), and similarly for a black run followed by a white run (`no_black_white_run_quarter`). So every word 1^r u with 1 ≤ |u| ≤ 4 and u starting white is excluded for r ≥ 9 (`no_black_run_ge9_len_le4`; the kit's `Rule30BlackRunBlocks` needs r ≥ 18 or 27 for its eight blocks), and every 1^r u with |u| ≤ 8 for r ≥ 18. **White runs.** Theorem W′ (`no_white_run_block`) excludes 0^r (1 :: v) as the eventual period from two finite kernel-checked certificates. It gives eight tails with sharper bounds than the catalog: r ≥ 12 for 1011, 10011, 11011, 101011 and 110011, r ≥ 20 for 111001, r ≥ 21 for 100011 and 111011 (the catalog: 49, 61 or 71). **An integer form of Q01.** One step of the kit's zero-boundary left half, read as a binary number, is F(Y) = ⌊Y/2⌋ XOR (Y OR 2Y), and the kit's open condition Q01, which excludes period 2, holds iff every natural number Y reaches an even number under some iterate of G = F∘F (`Q01_iff_integer`). F is tied to the kit's moving-frame map Φ(Y) = Y XOR (2Y OR 4Y) by Φ(Y) = 2F(Y) + (Y mod 2). Numerically every Y < 2^16 reaches an even number within 16 steps of G. None of this excludes period 2, 3 or 4: their words have no black run of length 9, and Q01 stays open. Direct AI involvement: Primary submission credits Renaud Bosdure; Gemini (Google); Claude (Anthropic); agent disclosure: Gemini 4 Argon (agy) with Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5). r1ContributionFamily.rationale: This record contributes a mathematical result whose canonical claim is: The source reports: Problem 1 asks whether the center column of rule 30 is ever eventually periodic. We prove three partial results in Lean, against the current kit. **Self-shielding.** By the kit's Lemma A* (`Rule30BlackRuns.black_shield`), a black run of length 9j in the center column forces the pattern (white, black)^j in columns 1..2j. This pattern shields itself: it moves two columns to the right every two steps without reading the cell on its right, so for 2j steps after the run the columns 1..2j depend only on the center column, and column 1 is determined for 4j steps instead of the 2j of the light cone. With masked Jen this halves the slope of the kit's Theorems B and D: if the center column is eventually P-periodic, it has no black run of length r < P followed by a white cell with 9⌈(P−r)/4⌉ ≤ r (`Rule30Submission.no_long_black_run_quarter`; the kit needs 9⌈(P−r+9)/2⌉ ≤ r), and similarly for a black run followed by a white run (`no_black_white_run_quarter`). So every word 1^r u with 1 ≤ |u| ≤ 4 and u starting white is excluded for r ≥ 9 (`no_black_run_ge9_len_le4`; the kit's `Rule30BlackRunBlocks` needs r ≥ 18 or 27 for its eight blocks), and every 1^r u with |u| ≤ 8 for r ≥ 18. **White runs.** Theorem W′ (`no_white_run_block`) excludes 0^r (1 :: v) as the eventual period from two finite kernel-checked certificates. It gives eight tails with sharper bounds than the catalog: r ≥ 12 for 1011, 10011, 11011, 101011 and 110011, r ≥ 20 for 111001, r ≥ 21 for 100011 and 111011 (the catalog: 49, 61 or 71). **An integer form of Q01.** One step of the kit's zero-boundary left half, read as a binary number, is F(Y) = ⌊Y/2⌋ XOR (Y OR 2Y), and the kit's open condition Q01, which excludes period 2, holds iff every natural number Y reaches an even number under some iterate of G = F∘F (`Q01_iff_integer`). F is tied to the kit's moving-frame map Φ(Y) = Y XOR (2Y OR 4Y) by Φ(Y) = 2F(Y) + (Y mod 2). Numerically every Y < 2^16 reaches an even number within 16 steps of G. None of this excludes period 2, 3 or 4: their words have no black run of length 9, and Q01 stays open. entry.description:
Left-Diagonal Defect Spectra, Sublinear Monochromatic Run Bounds, and Semigroup Saturation in Rule 30. The primary source reports: This submission presents Emerson Villafuerte's verified work on diagonal defect spectra and run bounds across 88 kernel-verified theorems.

Key results and clarifications:
1. Universal Black Run Bound: for all a >= 4, every black run on the center column satisfies L <= a - 2 (`black_run_center_le_ge4`), strictly improving Morales's linear bound L <= a. As noted in peer review, this bound is strictly stronger than the three-fifths bound of R30-20261025-0554f7 (L <= a - 2 Floor[(a - 1)/5]) at a = 4 (2 < 4) and a = 5 (3 < 5).
2. Recurrence Window: every interval [a, 2a - 2] holds a white cell (`exists_white_ge4`), contracting Morales's [a, 2a].
3. Conditional White Row Bound: diagonal defect theorems establish conditional bounds on alternating triangular preRow row blocks (`white_run_le_diag5`: L <= a - 5 whenever ell + 7 <= a). Per reviewer guidance, this is not an unconditional bound on center-column white runs, for which no bound L <= a - 5 holds since c(6) = c(7) = 0.
4. Diagonal Defect Spectrum: exact closed-form period determinations D_2(t+2) = false, D_3(t+2) = [t = 1 mod 2], D_4(t+2) = true, and D_5(t+3) = [t = 0 mod 2], with defect theorems bounding runs by a - j.
5. Preserved Foundation: Semigroup saturation excluding 22 infinite repeating-word families (8 white-run 0^q u, 14 black-run 1^r u), universal period-2 dichotomy, unconditional solutions of CQEmpty across all phases for period-4 words (0001, 0011, 0111) and period-3 (001), bounded-width Q001 (W <= 12), and depth-1000 sideways certifications.

All 88 headlines are kernel-checked with standard axioms only (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound), 0 sorry, 0 non-standard axioms. Full solution to Problems 1, 2, or 3 is not claimed. Direct AI involvement: Primary submission credits Emerson Villafuerte; Antigravity (Google DeepMind); agent disclosure: Antigravity (Google DeepMind). Further checking: This is a bounded partial result only, not a solution to any Rule30 Prize problem. Registry explicitly reports human review and kit incorporation, but novelty and scope still require comparison with the dated prior kit. Compare overlapping word families, bound improvements and antecedents exactly; independently inspect the actual submission and finite certificate scope. Keep only the new scoped contribution, not known background or numerical observations. The advertised a-2 bound improves the three-fifths bound only at a=4,5; title wording “sublinear” is not supported by those linear inequalities. The white a-5 bound is conditional and not a bound on all center runs.  Independently check correctness, novelty, priority, exact AI mathematical contribution and statement correspondence. Source-reported author/agent, kernel or registry checks are not an independent expert audit here; no downloaded proof artifact, certificate, program or macro was executed. Registry/submission dates are dated public observations; reconstruct any earlier public manuscript or artifact release before backdating. Retain provisional=1, low strict confidence, taxonomy unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.

entry.description:
Partial structural results toward Rule 30 Problem 1: a truncation bridge, first kernel-checked Q001 instances, and a coupled golden-mean source constraint. The primary source reports: **Result.** Partial results toward Problem 1, via the kit's left-half reductions `Q01` (period 2) and `Q001` (least period 3). A generic truncation bridge, `constrained_black_window`: a width-$d$ death bound $D$ forces a black cell at a depth in $(d, D+1]$ in *every* row whose column $-1$ matches a fixed pattern on a time-set forever  finite or infinite rows alike. Instances: `black_window_52` (a black cell in $(d, 97]$ for every $d \le 52$) and the period-3 `q001_black_window`. The first kernel-checked instances of `Q001`: `q001_cases_up_to_16`, `q001_width_le_16`. An equivalence upgrade, `q001_iff_finite_dies`: `Q001` holds iff every finitely supported zero-boundary start has column $-1$ white at some step $3j$. A coupled structural constraint: `no_two_by_two_black` (Rule 30 has no $2\times 2$ all-black block) and `source_no_vertical_11` (the adjacent-black source is $11$-free in time).

**New relative to the catalog.** The kit has no kernel-checked `Q001` instances (its evidence is a non-kernel C search); the truncation-bridge and black-window statements, and the coupled adjacent-black-source ($11$-free) structure, are absent from the catalog.

**Method.** Left-permutivity (the OR-latch $x_i = 1 \Rightarrow F(x)_i = x_{i-1} \oplus 1$) gives the no-$2\times2$ / $11$-free source in three lines. Triangular truncation turns any width-$d$ kernel death bound into an unconditional black-window statement for infinite constrained rows; the `Q001` instances are kernel-checked finite case analyses; `adjSrc_factor_le_fib` uses the elementary count of $11$-free words, $\mathrm{fib}(n+2)$.

**Not claimed.** No prize problem is solved; Problems 1-3 remain open. These are partial results toward the `Q01` / `Q001` reductions, not a proof of non-periodicity. The $\mathrm{fib}(n+2)$ factor-complexity bound is elementary and orthogonal to the prize: an upper bound on a *derived* sequence, whereas Problem 1 needs an unbounded *lower* bound on the center column itself. taxonomy.claim: The source reports: For each of 80 repeating words w of length 17 and 18, none of them in the kit's `Rule30StripCertificateTable`, the center column of rule 30 is not eventually w repeated (`Rule30Submission.not_eventuallyWord_words`), and no column of any configuration with a leftmost black cell reads w periodically from any time on (`Rule30Submission.words_general`). Correction: this replaces R30-20261022-70d23b, which counted all 80 words as new. Six were excluded before it: `0 1^16` and `0 1^17` in every column (`Rule30FiniteBlackRuns`); `0^15 1 1` and `0^16 1 1` for every nonzero finite configuration (`Rule30WhiteRunEight`, `Rule30FiniteWhiteRuns`); and `1 0^16` and `1 0^17` by our R30-20261022-c27323. So 74 words are new, and for two more only the statement for every configuration with a leftmost black cell is new. The Lean is unchanged apart from its docstring. The argument is Jen's, word by word: the K cells right of the column form a finite relaxation; after a few periods of the word, one more period maps its reachable set into itself while the next column takes a single value at every tick, so two adjacent columns are periodic, which the moving left edge forbids. Each word's finite fact is decided by the Lean kernel. Nothing is claimed for any word not listed, and this is not a solution of Problem 1. Current primary source reports: The platform now reports status Lean Verified, tags ['Human Verified'] and kit integration None. The bounded mathematical claim and original first-public date are unchanged; no Rule30 Prize resolution is inferred.

entry.description: Periodic temporal profiles of rule 30: pulse holes, source weights and rooted returns. The primary source reports: We study Boolean temporal profiles related by the rule 30 left-diagonal recurrence C(t+1) = A(t) XOR (B(t) OR C(t)). `Rule30Submission.pulse_source_weight` shows that a one-bit pulse in B makes the cyclic weight of its recovered source A equal to twice the rising-edge count of C, with an explicit correction of minus one, zero or one. `Rule30Submission.pulse_child_holes` shows that a pulse followed by a profile whose first positive black phase is L forces a child white exactly at phases 1 through L. For q-periodic profiles with q at least 4, `Rule30Submission.leftWindow_pulse_bound` identifies the resulting three first-black delays and bounds their doubled maximum contiguous-interval excess over slope 5/2 by 2q-5 + max(0,2L-5), attained at the phase just after the pulse. Separately, `Rule30Submission.rooted_chain_returns_bounded` proves that any infinite chain of q-periodic child triples starting with a white profile contains another white profile at an index from 1 through 2^(2q); the proof counts finite two-profile codes and recovers predecessors from a repeated pair. Reset existence and uniqueness (`Rule30Submission.child_exists`, `Rule30Submission.child_unique`), and explicit connections to actual rule 30 evolution after a common onset, are also proved. These are conditional profile statements. They neither establish finite-seed ancestry for arbitrary profiles nor decide eventual periodicity of the single-seed centre column. Direct AI involvement: Primary submission credits Gareth Herbert; Claude (Anthropic); GPT (OpenAI); agent disclosure: Claude Code with Claude Opus 5.5. entry.description: Finite-arc rotation codes beside a Rule 30 clock. The primary source reports: Suppose a Rule 30 row has its leftmost black cell at -L, with L a natural number, and column 0 is white at even times and black at odd times from time 0. We prove its visible neighbour x(1,2s) cannot eventually equal a binary finite-step coding of an irrational circle rotation when continued-fraction digits exceed 2^(r+1) arbitrarily late, with r supplied endpoint labels. A window-Jen bound forces frequent mismatches; finite pigeonhole and continuant determinant spacing contradict that bound. Arbitrary endpoint values are allowed because an irrational orbit visits each listed endpoint at most once. A concrete union of k half-open intervals has threshold 2^(2k+1), counting its 2k supplied labels. The proof formalizes the record's general-arc extension; earlier Sturmian/block-code exclusions cover special cases. No all-irrational rotation, eventual physical-clock restart or prize result is claimed. Constructive Backward Operators, the Period-3 NOR Wave Trichotomy, and Projective Orbit Laws for Zero-Boundary Stripe Primitive Roots. The primary source reports: Responding to the PR #45 review on R30-20261028-8abb51 ("97 is not on the ray of 13, and a rule that gives the primitive roots off the ray is the question that remains"), we formalize the structure of the stripe primitive roots in core Lean 4.35.0 (`Rule30ZeroBoundaryStripePrimitiveRoots`, 2.9 s, zero certificate tables):

1. Constructive O(K) Backward Operators (`bstep1`, `bstep0`, `B_shift`): Two-sided inverses of `fstep K . 1`, `fstep K . 0`, and `(fS K)^2` on `Fin (2^K)`, coinciding with `(orb_inv K 2 (W, 0)).1` (`B_shift_eq_orb_inv_two`) and satisfying `B_shift K (F_shift V) = V` (`B_shift_F_shift`).
2. 2-Step Backward Trichotomy & Period-3 NOR Wave (`primitive_or_clone_trichotomy`, `backward_nor_period_three`, `exists_F_shift_eq_iff`): For `W < 2^k` (`4 <= k <= K`), `(U, V) = (bstep1 K W, B_shift K W)` falls into three regimes: (0) Clone (`U < 2^(k-2) /\ V < 2^(k-4)`, `<-> exists V_0 < 2^(k-4), F_shift V_0 = W`, singling out `223`); (I) Type I Primitive (`U < 2^(k-2)` and `V = 1^infty` on `[k-2, K)`, singling out `201, 225, 253`); (II) Type II Primitive (`U = 1^infty` on `[k, K)` and `V_i = !(V_{i-1} || V_{i-2})` with strict period 3 `V_{i+3} = V_i`, singling out `13`, `97`, and nine 8-bit roots).
3. The `win3pow n = 3*2^n + 1` Shift-Template Law (`B_shift_win3pow_shift_13`): For all `n >= 2` and `K`, `B_shift K (win3pow n)` is the `(n-2)`-bit shift of `B_shift K 13` with `n` low ones; `n = 5` (`97`, shift 3) is the minimal shift preserving the period-3 NOR wave phase of `13` (`n = 2`).

entry.description:
An All-Time Forbidden Return-Gap Pattern in the Alternating-Driven Rule 30 Right Orbit. The primary source reports: We prove an all-time restriction on a driven subsystem that arises in the period-two case of Problem 1. Let `u R1` be the kit's sideways observation (`Rule30PeriodTwoSideways.u`) of the right half whose center boundary is driven by the alternating sequence $1,0,1,0,\ldots$, started from the right seed black only at position 1. Record the first-return gaps between consecutive black observations. Every gap is 3 or 5, the first three gaps are 5, and the gap sequence contains the factor $3,5,3,5,3,5,3$ at no index (`Rule30Submission.alternating_R1_no_3535353`). The factors $3,3$ and $3,5,5,3$ are excluded at every index as well.

Relative to the kit catalog and earlier submissions, which give eventual 3/5 spacing for the empty right seed and finite-window obstructions for an alternating center, the new content is the all-index exclusion of this seven-gap word for the one-cell right seed. The exclusions of $3,3$ and $3,5,5,3$ come from our earlier work and are not claimed as new.

Method: the odd-time driven right half is projected to an 18-cell window whose two unseen outer inputs are left free, giving a finite nondeterministic relaxation. A 2,040-state inductive invariant pool, 3,010 first-return edges, a 30-subset deterministic reader and a nine-state monitor show that no relaxed history realizes a forbidden factor; the kit's packed-prefix theorems transfer this to the actual orbit.

The Universal Backward Wave Cascade, Clone-Ray Disjointness, and 16-Ray All-Length Mortality for Zero-Boundary Stripe Prefixes. The primary source reports: Building on `Rule30ZeroBoundaryStripeStructure` and `Rule30ZeroBoundaryStripePrimitiveRoots`, we formalize `Rule30ZeroBoundaryStripeCascade` in core Lean 4.35.0 (~5.0 s, zero certificate tables):

1. The Universal 4-Stage Backward Wave Cascade (`bstep1_nor_period_three`, `typeI_step3_nor_wave`, `typeI_eight_bit_three_phases`, `wave_100_to_011_step1`, `wave_100_to_011_step0`, `wave_011_to_period6_step0`): Whenever `V.testBit i = true` for `i >= m`, `X = bstep1 K V` obeys the NOR recurrence `X_i = !(X_{i-1} || X_{i-2})` and locks into a period-3 `(100)^infty` wave. Thus every Type I primitive root enters the period-3 `(100)^infty` wave at backward step 3 (`bstep1 K (B_shift K W)`), with the three 8-bit Type I roots `201, 225, 253` realizing all three wave phases. One further backward step (`bstep1 K` or `bstep0 K`) maps any `(100)^infty` wave to its bitwise complement `(011)^infty` (period 3), and the next step (`bstep0 K`) doubles the spatial period from 3 to 6, locking into `(000101)^infty` (`wave_011_to_period6_step0`).
2. entry.description: Failure of direct finiteness for group algebras in every odd characteristic. The primary source reports: For every odd prime p p , we construct a finitely presented group G p G_{p} and elements a , b , c ∈ 𝔽 p ​ [ G p ] a,b,c\in\mathbb{F}_{p}[G_{p}] such that a ​ b = 1 ab=1 , a ​ c = 0 ac=0 , and c ≠ 0 c\neq 0 . Thus 𝔽 p ​ [ G p ] \mathbb{F}_{p}[G_{p}] , and the group algebra over every field of characteristic p p , fails to be directly finite. The construction combines a single exceptional self-product pair with signed bipartite cancellation. New integer matching data realize the exceptional self-intersection while retaining a strict squared-word decay estimate. We verify the adaptations needed for the earlier bounded-path and planar-localization arguments. A minimal disk picture protects the identity coefficient of c c , so the proof does not require torsion-freeness. entry.anchor_claim: The source reports: . We consider the Robin Laplacian on a planar exterior domain with a negative boundary parameter. For a negative boundary parameter of a sufficiently large absolute value this operator has at least two negative eigenvalues below the bottom of the essential spectrum. We prove that under a fixed area constraint and convexity assumption on the bounded complement of the exterior domain the second Robin eigenvalue is maximized by the exterior of the disk. The inequality is strict for every exterior of a non-circular domain whenever the comparison disk has a negative second eigenvalue. The proof modifies the parallel-coordinate method by allowing the angular phase of a trial function to vary with the distance from the boundary. This result resolves the first item in [ KL24 , Conjecture 1.2] by the authors under an additional convexity assumption. Relaxing the convexity and the perimeter constraint remain open problems.

challengeContext.anchorClaim: The source reports: . We study two families of moduli spaces of sheaves attached to the node, namely the punctual Hilbert schemes of the non-reduced plane curve x u ​ y v = 0 x^{u}y^{v}=0 , and the punctual Quot schemes of the module 𝕜 ​ [ [ x ] ] u ⊕ 𝕜 ​ [ [ y ] ] v \Bbbk[[x]]^{u}\oplus\Bbbk[[y]]^{v} over the reduced node x ​ y = 0 xy=0 . We compute their motivic generating functions for all u , v u,v and over every field. Both are specializations of a single rational function whose numerator counts matrices by rank, and they are related by the substitution 𝕃 ↦ Q ​ 𝕃 \mathbb{L}\mapsto Q\mathbb{L} . This proves the Hilb–Quot correspondence for the node with independent ranks on the two branches. The main geometric ingredient is an elementary modification of an ideal along a branch of the curve, whose fibres are affine spaces of dimension equal to a contact length. We also construct stratifications of the Hilbert schemes into products of affine spaces and tori, and we formulate a branchwise Hilb–Quot–HOMFLY conjecture, which we test on the colored Hopf link.

entry.description: Proofs of strong forms of the Bovdi--Geche universality conjecture and a complex analogue. The primary source reports: . We prove two universality theorems for neural networks consisting of a single neuron. First we prove a strong form of the Bovdi–Geche universality conjecture on neurons over finite fields, where the activation function is a certain modification of the discrete logarithm, using the Weil bound on multiplicative character sums over finite fields. Then we show a generalisation of Aizenberg’s universality theorem for complex binary neurons with a weight vector independent of the target function, positively answering another question in the literature. The proof of the latter uses an equidistribution theorem for the dilates of certain maps into tori. entry.description: A Stochastic LineseArch Method (SLAM) for Minimizing Expectation Residuals: Weakening Boundedness of Gradient. The primary source reports: We establish convergence guarantees for the Stochastic LineseArch Method ( SLAM ) proposed and analyzed in [ 1 ] for nonconvex composite stochastic optimization, retaining the iteration and sample complexity orders of the original analysis assuming neither the boundedness of true gradients nor the Lipschitz continuity of the convex nonsmooth term r r . ChatGPT was used to assist in developing a key intermediate result. Under uniformly Lipschitz continuous and unbiased sampled gradients with uniformly bounded variance with mini-batch sizes proportional to the iteration budget, SLAM achieves an iteration complexity 𝒪 ⁡ ( ϵ − 2 ) \mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{-2}) and a sample complexity 𝒪 ⁡ ( ϵ − 4 ) \mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{-4}) for obtaining an iterate whose expected proximal-gradient residual norm is at most ϵ \epsilon . entry.description: Special cycles and Picard groups of Baily--Borel compactifications. The primary source reports: . In this paper, we answer two basic questions concerning algebraic cycles on orthogonal Shimura varieties attached to lattices. First, we prove that Kudla’s special cycles and Heegner cycles have the same rational span in every codimension. This fills a gap in the codimension-one argument of [ 2 , Remark 2.4] , pointed out by Bruinier–Zuffetti [ 5 ] . Second, in dimension at least ten, we prove that the rational Picard group of the Baily–Borel compactification is generated by the Hodge class. The proof of the second result reduces, via isotropic induction on the discriminant form, to the K3-type case treated in our previous work. Direct AI involvement: Primary paper disclosure (source-attributed excerpts):  our work in [ 10 ] . The idea of using isotropic subgroups of the discriminant form to reduce questions about general lattices to the K3-type case was discussed extensively during that earlier work. LLM was used in the preparation of this paper. The LLM assisted with the local orbit criterion in Lemma 3.1 , a local analogue of Eichler’s criterion. It also suggested the key idea of using a finite family of overlattices whose pullbacks jointly span the rational Picard group, rather than seeking a reduction through a single lattice. This idea is implemented in Proposition 5.4 ; the resulting spanning statement is then used with Proposition 5.6 and our earlier result in [ 10 ] . The LLM was also used as a writing aid to improve the language and readability of the manuscript. The authors have reviewed and verified all arguments and take full responsibility for the content of the paper. entry.description: Crescent configurations in three dimensions. The primary source reports: . A crescent configuration of n n points in ℝ d \mathbb{R}^{d} is a set in general position whose distinct pairwise distances have multiplicities 1 , … , n − 1 1,\ldots,n-1 . We construct such a configuration in ℝ 3 \mathbb{R}^{3} for every n ≥ 3 n\geq 3 , giving a uniform bound of three for the minimum dimension. The proof uses equally spaced parameters on a short circular helix and Rolle’s theorem. For a positive integer k k , let f ⁡ ( k ) f(k) be the minimum number of distinct nonempty subset sums of a zero-sum-free k k -element set, where the minimum is taken over all finite abelian groups. We prove f ⁡ ( k ) ≥ k 2 2 − 13 ​ k ​ log ⁡ ( k + 1 ) − 116 ​ k . f(k)\geq\frac{k^{2}}{2}-13k\log(k+1)-116k. Together with the classical upper bound, this gives f ⁡ ( k ) = k 2 / 2 + O ⁡ ( k ​ log ⁡ k ) f(k)=k^{2}/2+O(k\log k) , with the optimal leading coefficient. As a consequence, the Olson constant of every finite abelian group G G satisfies Ol ⁡ ( G ) ≤ 2 ​ | G | + O ⁡ ( log ⁡ | G | ) \Ol(G)\leq\sqrt{2|G|}+O(\log|G|) . The argument combines a triangular lower bound for repeated supports, a count using blocks of two and three copies, and a greedy expansion argument. entry.description: Backward Pseudolocality of $G_2$-Laplacian Flow. The primary source reports: . In this paper, we establish a new estimate on the time-derivative of pointed Nash entropy and use it to give a new proof of backward pseudolocality for Ricci flow. The proof does not rely on Bamler’s compactness theorem and structure theory concerning limits of Ricci flows. Our methods also work for other reasonable geometric flows, like the G 2 G_{2} -Laplacian, at a scale depending on its deviation from Ricci flow and its scalar curvature. entry.description: Order Maintenance in Worst-Case Constant Time, Verified. The primary source reports: Order maintenance asks for a data structure that keeps a sequence of elements under insertions and deletions and tells which of two elements comes first. We give an algorithm that performs each operation in worst-case constant time, and verify it in Lean 4. The difficulty is to change labels gradually while queries and further insertions continue. The algorithm, assembled from published components, never relabels the members of a full unit in place: they move into fresh neighbouring units. Small groups keep element labels short; groups are collected into larger chunks, which keep accepting insertions while they wait their turn for a shared top tree; and the top tree never changes a label it has assigned. We implement the algorithm as a program for a random-access machine (RAM) deeply embedded in Lean, whose interpreter counts every instruction and allocates a zero-filled array in one step, and prove that the program answers every query as a simple reference specification does and that each operation takes at most a fixed number of steps, independent of the number of elements and of the history. The machine treats arithmetic on unbounded natural numbers as one step, and on such a machine a step bound alone is weak, so we also prove that after t t operations no value the machine has computed has more than O ⁡ ( log ⁡ t ) O(\log t) bits, and that the program runs unchanged, with the same answers and step counts, on a machine whose words have that many bits. A verified translation through an intermediate language connects the high-level proofs to the machine program and preserves step counts exactly, so the interpreter is the only cost model to trust; the development has about 78,000 lines of Lean. Rust code transpiled from the program agrees with the machine semantics on all tested traces, and an unverified native implementation shows the algorithm’s practical cost. entry.description: Transverse rational curves and the homogeneity of contact Fano manifolds. The primary source reports: . We prove that every smooth complex projective contact Fano manifold is homogeneous under its connected contact automorphism group. The argument extends and simplifies the incidence method of our earlier proof of the LeBrun–Salamon conjecture. After the classical reductions, balanced transverse rational maps through every point yield tangent sections extending across the nodal boundary. These establish irreducibility and nonlinearity of the general variety of minimal rational tangents associated with contact lines, enabling Hwang’s descent theorem to produce global vector fields generating the tangent bundle. Consequences include very ampleness of the contact line bundle, embeddedness of every balanced rational map, Kähler–Einstein existence, K-polystability, and the LeBrun–Salamon conjecture. Direct AI involvement: Primary paper disclosure (source-attributed excerpts): contact homogeneity. The metric and twistor consequences follow afterwards. The propagation, smoothness and homogeneity criteria are formulated independently of the contact structure. AI declaration. ChatGPT was used solely as an auxiliary tool for literature searches, language editing, and preliminary checks of mathematical constructions and arguments. challengeContext.anchorClaim: The source reports: . We prove that every smooth complex projective contact Fano manifold is homogeneous under its connected contact automorphism group. The argument extends and simplifies the incidence method of our earlier proof of the LeBrun–Salamon conjecture. After the classical reductions, balanced transverse rational maps through every point yield tangent sections extending across the nodal boundary. These establish irreducibility and nonlinearity of the general variety of minimal rational tangents associated with contact lines, enabling Hwang’s descent theorem to produce global vector fields generating the tangent bundle. Consequences include very ampleness of the contact line bundle, embeddedness of every balanced rational map, Kähler–Einstein existence, K-polystability, and the LeBrun–Salamon conjecture.

entry.description: Sharp dimension bounds for right-angled hyperbolic polytopes. The primary source reports: We determine the largest dimensions in which right-angled hyperbolic polytopes of finite volume can exist. The dimension is at most eight in general, and at most four when all vertices lie at infinity. Both bounds are attained, improving the previously known upper bounds of twelve and six. Our proofs use elementary properties of hyperbolic polytopes together with bounds for configurations of points on spheres. entry.description: Meromorphic order from Taylor coefficients, least singular values of Hankel matrices and rational approximants. The primary source reports: We introduce a natural notion of generalized order for entire and meromorphic functions and express it in terms of their Taylor coefficients. More precisely, one formula uses the least singular values of Hankel matrices of the coefficients, and the other uses their determinants. These formulas generalize the classical coefficient formula for the order of entire functions and its extensions by Edrei and Sheremeta. The proof combines a theorem of Pommerenke with a bound for the Nevanlinna characteristic that results from a convergence theorem for rational approximants introduced by Prokhorov. We also characterize the largest class of growth scales for which the associated generalized order is well-behaved. entry.description: The maximum number of triangles in regular graphs. The primary source reports: We determine the maximum number of triangles in n n -vertex k k -regular graphs and characterize all extremal graphs for all admissible orders when k k is odd and for an explicit range of orders when k k is even. For even k k , we also give explicit lower and upper bounds for the remaining orders. As a consequence, we obtain a lower bound on the number of independent sets of size three in k k -regular graphs and characterize all equality cases. entry.description: Guaranteed indirect delivery in directed networks: The joint extremal function and explicit attaining constructions. The primary source reports: A messenger and a pursuer move alternately on a finite loopless directed graph, with complete information and waiting permitted. The messenger moves first and wins upon reaching a designated recipient, before interception there. We determine the maximum number M ⁡ ( n , m ) M(n,m) of ordered nonadjacent source–recipient pairs for which delivery is guaranteed against every initial pursuer position, among graphs with n n vertices and m m arcs. We give the exact value and an explicit attaining graph for every admissible pair ( n , m ) (n,m) . For n ≥ 12 n\geq 12 , a piecewise formula describes sparse growth, the interval 2 ​ n ≤ m ≤ n ⁡ ( n − 3 ) 2n\leq m\leq n(n-3) in which every missing pair can be guaranteed, a dense staircase, and the zero range above n ⁡ ( n − 2 ) n(n-2) . Complete finite tables cover smaller orders. The proofs combine degree and support bounds, local strategy composition, protected routing, and constructions in the missing-arc graph. Finite exceptional cases use explicit strategy certificates and complete computational exclusions. Reproducible programs and certificates accompany the paper; a Lean development verifies the complete formula for n ≥ 12 n\geq 12 and m ≥ 24 m\geq 24 , the claimed scores of prescribed constructions at every admissible pair, and further finite upper bounds. Its remaining obligations are stated separately. entry.description: On the Tur\'an Number of the Cartesian Product of Two Stars. The primary source reports: We study the Turán number of the Cartesian product of two stars, a family whose order of magnitude is known. For most pairs of star sizes, we determine the leading coefficient exactly. In the remaining congruence class, we give explicit lower and upper bounds for the coefficient at the leading scale. Our lower bounds use blowups of polarity graphs, and our upper bounds use structural estimates on neighbourhoods. entry.description: The M\'ezard-Parisi formula. The primary source reports: This paper proves the Mézard–Parisi formula for the free energy of random K K -sat and diluted p p -spin models with even p p , completing an approach developed in earlier work of the author and collaborators. The upper bound was established by Franz and Leone. Here the matching lower bound is proved for a general class of diluted models under symmetry and integrability assumptions. The main new contribution is a proof of an approximate form of the Mézard–Parisi reproducibility hypothesis without assuming that the overlap distribution has finite support. Direct AI involvement: Primary paper disclosure (source-attributed excerpts): ] established the exact threshold for all sufficiently large k k , confirming the one-step replica-symmetry-breaking prediction. Acknowledgement on the use of AI. The proof in this paper was found by ChatGPT Astra. I asked it to look for a new perturbation in the argument of [ 31 ] and try to simplify the induction. It returned an initial version of the argument developed below. I have read, checked, and rewritten the proof. ChatGPT Astra and Claude Fable assisted me with the rewriting. A few days after the proof presented here was found, OpenAI released another proof of the Mézard–Parisi formula in [ 24 ] . That proof appears to follow a different approach. Acknowledgements. I would like to thank Giorgio Parisi for his help in preparing this paper. 2 Models and main result 2.1 The diluted models Fix an integer K ≥ 2 K\geq 2 . entry.description: The number of $C_4$-free graphs. The primary source reports: Erdős, Frankl and Rödl showed that the number of graphs on n n vertices with no copy of a non-bipartite graph H H is 2 ( 1 + o ⁡ ( 1 ) ) ​ ex ​ ( n , H ) 2^{(1+o(1))\mathrm{ex}(n,H)} , whereas Morris and Saxton showed that this fails for C 6 C_{6} . Answering a question of Erdős, we prove that the number of C 4 C_{4} -free graphs on n n vertices is 2 ( 1 + o ⁡ ( 1 ) ) ​ ex ​ ( n , C 4 ) 2^{(1+o(1))\mathrm{ex}(n,C_{4})} . entry.description: Solutions to several problems on infinite sumset configurations. The primary source reports: . We resolve a number of the problems collected by Kra, Moreira, Richter and Robertson in their survey Problems on infinite sumset configurations in the integers and beyond . Our main result is that in every countably infinite abelian group, every set of positive upper Banach density contains a sumset B 1 + ⋯ + B k B_{1}+\dots+B_{k} of k k infinite sets, for every k k ; the proof uses the Kronecker factor, but no higher-order Host–Kra structure theory, nilsystems of step greater than one, or nilspaces. entry.description: Optimal AFEM convergence for any bulk parameter smaller than one. The primary source reports: . We prove rate-optimal convergence of the standard adaptive finite element method with conforming Lagrange elements for the Poisson problem for Dörfler marking with any bulk parameter θ ∈ ( 0 , 1 ) \theta\in(0,1) . This removes the smallness restriction on the bulk parameter that has persisted in the classical theory of optimal adaptive finite element methods. Direct AI involvement: Primary paper disclosure (source-attributed excerpts):  is part of a longer-term project of the authors on adaptive finite element methods. During the final stage of the present work, an extended interactive discussion between Johannes Storn and OpenAI’s ChatGPT, motivated in particular by our recent results on L 2 L^{2} and Ritz projection stability, led to an initial framework for the proof. Since the mathematical ideas developed through a long sequence of questions, suggestions, and revisions, we do not attempt to separate the individual contributions of the human and AI participants to this stage. entry.description: Optimal self-orthogonal binary linear codes. The primary source reports: We complete the determination of the minimum possible length of eight-dimensional binary self-orthogonal codes with given minimum distance. For dimension nine we give exact values and bounds for minimum distance at most 64 64 . By exploiting the geometric reformulation of linear codes as multisets of points, we fully redo the classification for dimension at most seven in a simplified and computer-free manner. As a by-product we prove the non-existence of [ 93 , 9 , 44 ] 2 [93,9,44]_{2} codes and show several divisibility results for putative optimal nine-dimensional binary codes. Keywords: self-orthogonal codes ⋅ \cdot linear codes ⋅ \cdot Griesmer bound ⋅ \cdot Galois geometry 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification: Primary 94B05; Secondary 51E21, 94B27, 94B65 Direct AI involvement: Proofs that do not use exhaustive computer enumerations of codes were found with AI tools e.g. for the cases [ 97 , 8 , 46 ] 2 [97,8,46]_{2} and [ 90 , 8 , 42 ] 2 [90,8,42]_{2} . They use rational certificates and computer-generated complete lists of candidate integer weight distributions. The proofs have been checked by independent AI reviews and exact computer checks, but not yet by a human expert. They will be made available, with the checking scripts, in the GitHub repository of Hirotaka Shimizu at https://github.com/yygotm?tab=repositories . We remark that there exist exactly six non-equivalent [ 119 , 7 , 58 ] 2 [119,7,58]_{2} SO codes with maximum weight 76 76 . Five of them violate A 66 = 0 A_{66}=0 or A 62 ≤ 20 A_{62}\leq 20 . entry.description: A lifted entropy splitting lemma and applications. The primary source reports: We give a matrix lifting of the entropy-splitting theorem of Csiszár, Körner, Lovász, Marton, and Simonyi, and show several applications. We use it to prove the Cartesian-product inequality conjectured by Sinjorgo and Sotirov for the generalized Lovász theta number, and we also answer the saturation and convexification questions of Carli Silva, Coutinho, Oliveira, and Tunçel on the same theme. For the strong Hoffman bound, we answer a question of Wocjan, Elphick, and Darbari concerning orthogonal rank, and show that optimization over matrix weights gives exactly the ceiling of the theta number of the complement. Finally, we extend the lifting to diagonally invariant cones of positive semidefinite matrices, giving a proof of a conjecture by Kuryatnikova, Sotirov, and Vera, and giving a short proof, for all graphs, of a theta-based weakening of Fajtlowicz’s graph-energy conjecture. The authors worked on distilling the key steps and found the combination of entropy splitting and matrix lifting presented in Sections 1 and 4 . entry.description: Three-dimensional QCA that are not stably circuits. The primary source reports: . We prove that the three-dimensional chiral ℤ p \mathbb{Z}_{p} Clifford quantum cellular automata of Haah and of Sun–Yang–Wang–Tantivasadakarn–Chen are, for every odd prime p p , not finite-depth quantum circuits, even after tensoring with arbitrary ancillary degrees of freedom and composing with translations. Previously such statements were known only inside the Clifford category. As a consequence, the group of three-dimensional QCA modulo stabilized circuits and translations is not finitely generated. The key ingredient is a new invariant of invertible subalgebras, which we conjecture to be the square of the total quantum dimension of the hosted anyon theory, modulo rational squares. challengeContext.anchorClaim: The source reports: . We prove that the three-dimensional chiral ℤ p \mathbb{Z}_{p} Clifford quantum cellular automata of Haah and of Sun–Yang–Wang–Tantivasadakarn–Chen are, for every odd prime p p , not finite-depth quantum circuits, even after tensoring with arbitrary ancillary degrees of freedom and composing with translations. Previously such statements were known only inside the Clifford category. As a consequence, the group of three-dimensional QCA modulo stabilized circuits and translations is not finitely generated. The key ingredient is a new invariant of invertible subalgebras, which we conjecture to be the square of the total quantum dimension of the hosted anyon theory, modulo rational squares.

entry.description: Division and noetherianity in quasianalytic Denjoy-Carleman classes. The primary source reports: . We show that the local rings of quasianalytic Denjoy–Carleman classes need not be Noetherian. More precisely, we construct quasianalytic Denjoy–Carleman classes C M C^{M} whose local rings C M ​ ( ℝ d , 0 ) C^{M}(\mathbb{R}^{d},0) are not Noetherian for any d ≥ 2 d\geq 2 . Conversely, we exhibit quasianalytic classes whose local rings in dimension two are regular and Noetherian. Our approach is based on the problem of exact division: if f = φ ​ g f=\varphi g , where f ∈ C M f\in C^{M} , φ \varphi is real-analytic, and g ∈ C ∞ g\in C^{\infty} , under which conditions does it follow that g ∈ C M g\in C^{M} ? We introduce a quantitative scale-growth condition on the defining weight sequence M M and prove that exact division holds in two variables whenever this condition is sufficiently strong relative to the rate at which the nonreal branches of the complex zero set of φ \varphi approach the real plane. We also construct quasianalytic weight sequences with prescribed growth thresholds and establish corresponding counterexamples to exact division. These yield nonclosed principal ideals and, consequently, non-Noetherian local rings. challengeContext.anchorClaim: The source reports: . We show that the local rings of quasianalytic Denjoy–Carleman classes need not be Noetherian. More precisely, we construct quasianalytic Denjoy–Carleman classes C M C^{M} whose local rings C M ​ ( ℝ d , 0 ) C^{M}(\mathbb{R}^{d},0) are not Noetherian for any d ≥ 2 d\geq 2 . Conversely, we exhibit quasianalytic classes whose local rings in dimension two are regular and Noetherian. Our approach is based on the problem of exact division: if f = φ ​ g f=\varphi g , where f ∈ C M f\in C^{M} , φ \varphi is real-analytic, and g ∈ C ∞ g\in C^{\infty} , under which conditions does it follow that g ∈ C M g\in C^{M} ? We introduce a quantitative scale-growth condition on the defining weight sequence M M and prove that exact division holds in two variables whenever this condition is sufficiently strong relative to the rate at which the nonreal branches of the complex zero set of φ \varphi approach the real plane. We also construct quasianalytic weight sequences with prescribed growth thresholds and establish corresponding counterexamples to exact division. These yield nonclosed principal ideals and, consequently, non-Noetherian local rings.

entry.description: Thin ends and topological spanning trees. The primary source reports: . Halin conjectured in 1964 that every connected graph has an end-faithful spanning tree. He proved this for countable graphs, but in the early 1990s Seymour and Thomas and, independently, Thomassen found uncountable counterexamples. Both are infinitely connected and hence one-ended, and their unique end has uncountable degree (i.e. contains uncountably many pairwise disjoint rays). Several authors have since asked how much of the conjecture survives. Diestel asked in 1992 whether a graph has an end-faithful spanning tree as soon as all its one-ended connected subgraphs have one; by a theorem of Polat, this would give end-faithful spanning trees in all connected graphs whose ends have countable degree. Diestel and Kühn introduced topological spanning trees, a topological variant of end-faithful spanning trees that exists in every one-ended connected graph, and asked in 2004 whether every connected graph has one. And Carmesin asked in 2019 whether every graph has a spanning tree that is end-faithful at least for its thin ends, the ends of finite degree. We answer all three questions in the negative. We show that the uncountably chromatic graph from an earlier note of ours on a problem of Erdős and Hajnal has only ends of countable degree, each dominated by only countably many vertices, yet it has neither an end-faithful nor a topological spanning tree. A refinement of this graph moreover has no spanning tree that contains a ray from every end of degree 1 1 . Direct AI involvement: Primary paper disclosure (source-attributed excerpts): {G} [ 1 ] . entry.description: The velocity is deterministic in random walk in 2-valued i.i.d. random environment. The primary source reports: We prove that the limiting velocity for (nearest-neighbour) random walk in i.i.d. random environment is deterministic when the local environment is supported on two points. No ellipticity is assumed. The proof uses a clever adaption (suggested by ChatGPT) of coupling arguments previously developed by the authors. It extends to i.i.d. environments where the local environments are mixtures of two such points. entry.description: Classical communication over quantum channels: does entanglement help in nature?. The primary source reports: Can entangling codewords across independent uses of a quantum channel improve the rate of classical communication? An old conjecture states that there is no such entanglement advantage for all channels. Although Hastings’s result and follow-up works disproved this conjecture, it turns out that enormous dimension is required to construct a channel where entanglement enhances classical communication. This indicates that there might be no entanglement advantage for many physical channels, or for all low dimensional channels. Motivated by recent progress on (generalized) amplitude damping channels, we propose a general Schur-weighted block entropy inequality, and show that there is no entanglement advantage for all phase-covariant channels including multi-level amplitude damping channels, generalized dephasing channels, and damping-dephasing channels. As a by-product, we also recover the recently established result that there is no entanglement advantage for all qubit channels. Although Hastings’s result and follow-up works disproved this conjecture, it turns out that enormous dimension is required to construct a channel where entanglement enhances classical communication. This indicates that there might be no entanglement advantage for many physical channels, or for all low dimensional channels. Motivated by recent progress on (generalized) amplitude damping channels, we propose a general Schur-weighted block entropy inequality, and show that there is no entanglement advantage for all phase-covariant channels including multi-level amplitude damping channels, generalized dephasing channels, and damping-dephasing channels. As a by-product, we also recover the recently established result that there is no entanglement advantage for all qubit channels.
